Obtaining RCT data may be costly, unethical, time-consuming, impossible

assignment bias in the sample
Imagine a clinical trial for an advanced stage cancer.
When contemporary medicine (say drug A) is not helping, the acting clinician may forward the patient to a
running clinical trial (for drug B).
After the trial, we should compare outcomes, i.e., E[Y|B] vs. E[Y|A].
Because we did not randomly assign the new (and old) drug to patients, the expectation (E) is not calculated
over the same distribution!
Typically, patients that were forwarded to drug B, were already in a worse state.
As such, we may severely underestimate the efficacy of drug B.
A variety of methods have been proposed to address this selection bias
Weighting approaches, synthetic control, …
Most of these try to ‘balance’ the control and treatment sample
I.e., to make their distributions similar
